prompt: request.port returns a wrong number when the Host header has no port: for the IPv6 host '[::1]' it returns 1, and for '127.0.0.1' it returns 127, where it should return null. Fix the request.port getter so that it returns the port, as a number, only when the Host header (or, when there is no Host header, the HTTP/2 ':authority' header) ends with ':' followed by digits, and null otherwise. For example: 'example.com:80' gives 80, 'example.com:443' gives 443, '[::1]:80' gives 80, '[::1]' gives null, '127.0.0.1' gives null, 'example.com' gives null, 'localhost:3000' gives 3000, an ':authority' of '1.2.3.4:80' with no Host header gives 80, and no Host or ':authority' header gives null.
requirement: Request.prototype.port returns parseInt of the trailing ':<digits>' of the Host header, falling back to the ':authority' header when Host is absent; when that value does not end with ':' followed by one or more digits (including IPv6 hosts without a port, IPv4 hosts without a port, plain hostnames and a missing header) it returns null. IPv6 hosts with a port ('[::1]:443') return the port.

oracle.approved_by: Arshad Ahmed Shaik (delegated approval; AI technical review by Claude)

acceptance_criteria.criterion: a Host with a trailing port returns that port as a number: 'example.com:80' gives 80, 'localhost:3000' gives 3000, '[::1]:443' gives 443
a Host without a port returns null, including '[::1]', '127.0.0.1' and 'example.com'
with no Host header the ':authority' header is used ('1.2.3.4:80' gives 80); with neither header the port is null
